note: Adapted from the species description of Chhotani (1997), originally in English; only the soldier is recorded for this species, neither the alate nor the worker being described in the original; the length of the hind femur is omitted owing to OCR damage; synonymic lists, figure numbers and distribution records are not translated.

sections.label: Soldier
sections.text: Head and rostrum brown with a smoky tinge; antennae dark brown; thoracic dorsum pale brown; femora smoky brown, tibiae and tarsi much paler than the femora; abdominal tergites smoky brown, sternites pale. Head and body dorsum without long setae, venter densely setose; one short seta on each side of the occiput, one on each side of the rostrum, 2 short setae on the body, a few setae at the apex of the rostrum. Body length 4.8–5.0 mm. Head capsule pear-shaped, strongly constricted behind the antennae (1.85–2.00 mm including the rostrum, 1.25–1.35 mm excluding the rostrum, maximum width 1.20–1.30 mm, width at the constriction 0.80–0.90 mm; head constriction index, i.e. width at the constriction/head width, 0.66–0.69); posterior part strongly raised (posterior bulge 0.45–0.62 mm, head bulge index 0.33–0.49); in lateral view strongly incurved behind the rostrum, occiput raised, without rostral swelling; posterior margin strongly convex. Eyes situated behind the antennae, small, suboval, white, indistinct. Rostrum short, conical; about half the head length (0.60–0.65 mm long, rostrum length/head length index 0.44–0.48); apex raised in lateral view. Antennae very long, 14-segmented; 3rd segment twice the length of the 2nd, only slightly longer than the 4th. Mandibles reduced, each with a dark brown, long spine-like process. Thoracic nota with a fine white median longitudinal line. Pronotum saddle-shaped; half as long as wide (0.35 mm long, 0.75 mm wide). Hind femur slender and long.
